primitive-functions

primitive-functions / FunctionApi

Interface: FunctionApi ​

The typed HTTP profile, generated from the platform's OpenAPI document. Its namespaces mirror the operation ids: agentSessions, analytics, blobBuckets, channels, collections, configVars, connections, databaseTypeConfigs, databases, db3, documents, email, functions, groups, integrations, invitations, locks, notifications, prompts, resourceMetadata, secrets, usage, users. Methods take one options object carrying the operation's path parameters, query parameters, request headers (under their wire names) and body.

Generated from the same operations as the runtime profile, so a method that type-checks is a method the platform publishes — and a missing path parameter or a missing required header is a compile error rather than a TypeError at invoke time. Every call runs with the app's own SYSTEM authority: the invocation gate was the authorization. The two namespaces the gateway does not admit are still declared: they exist, they answer the gateway's structured denial, and hiding them would make a route's availability look like a typo. Those are databaseTypeConfigs whole, and functions except for functions.start — the nested-start door admits by name, which ctx.functions.start calls. functions.invoke stays refused: same-run composition is an import.

The key of an agent prompt (kind = "agent") in this app.

Initial participants (they send, answer and upload): existing users of this app, distinct, not the caller. Together with viewers at most 50.

Free text an app groups sessions by; 1 to 256 characters.

string

body.userId? ​

string

Whose session: the member who owns it. Omitted means the caller. An app owner or admin, or a server function run with no caller or one an app owner or admin invoked, may name another member; a run with no caller must name one (FUNCTION_SUBJECT_REQUIRED). An ordinary member's run may name another member only when its function declares users:readAny (on a read) or users:actAsAny (on a call that acts as them), and a run an agent drives never may (SUBJECT_USER_FORBIDDEN).

body.variables? ​

Record<string, unknown>

The session's variables, validated against the agent's inputSchema; at most 16 KiB of JSON. Absent reads as {}.

body.viewers? ​

string[]

Initial viewers (they read the session's db3): existing users of this app, distinct, in neither list twice, not the caller.

listEvents() ​

analytics.listEvents — GET /analytics/events. List analytics events

Pages the app's raw event feed, newest first, with the standard list envelope: rows in items, the next page by nextCursor, the end at hasMore: false. Among events of the same second the order is fixed by every returned field. A page ends on a whole second where it can, so it can hold fewer than limit rows while hasMore is true. A walk covers the window as it stood at its first page: an event recorded later is not returned by that walk. Paging through events that keep arriving returns each event at most once, except within a single second that holds more than limit events, where a late-arriving row can repeat (events have no id and one-second timestamps, so the walk continues inside such a second by offset). A nextCursor is accepted only with the same windowDays, filters and testUsers. The numbered-page parameter page and the keys rows, page, page_size, total_rows and _timing are deprecated and removed in the first breaking release after 2027-02-15.

Parameters ​
args ​
body ​

{ field?: string; fields?: string[]; kind?: "members" | "scalar" | "text" | "vector"; members?: boolean; model: string; name?: string; on?: "server" | "device" | "both"; text?: { prefix?: number[]; tokenizer?: "unicode61" | "porter"; weights?: Record<string, number>; }; unique?: boolean; vector?: { distance?: "cos" | "l2"; index?: "exact" | { codesize?: number; mode: "ann"; nbucket?: number; quantizer?: "pq" | "opq" | "bq"; }; }; }

body.field? ​

string

body.fields? ​

string[]

body.kind? ​

"members" | "scalar" | "text" | "vector"

What the index is; scalar when omitted (members with members: true).

body.members? ​

boolean

true registers a member index on field, a string-set field: the same as kind: "members". It takes no fields, unique or name.

body.model ​

string

body.name? ​

string

A scalar index's only.

body.on? ​

"server" | "device" | "both"

Where the index lives; both for a scalar or text index, server for a member index and device for a vector index when omitted. A member or text index may live anywhere and a vector index on the device; a unique index needs server or both. A text index placed server or both is built from the model's records within this request. Change it by dropping the index and registering it again.

body.text? ​

{ prefix?: number[]; tokenizer?: "unicode61" | "porter"; weights?: Record<string, number>; }

A text index's options. Each is optional; any other key is refused DB3_INDEX_INVALID.

body.text.prefix? ​

number[]

Prefix lengths to index, each 1 to 32 and at most 8 of them, so a prefix search on words that long reads the index directly. None by default.

body.text.tokenizer? ​

"unicode61" | "porter"

How words are split and folded: unicode61 (diacritics folded, the default) or porter (English stems on top).

body.text.weights? ​

Record<string, number>

A positive weight per covered field, 1 by default: a match in a heavier field ranks higher.

body.unique? ​

boolean

A scalar index's only: a write giving two live records the same key is refused.

body.vector? ​

{ distance?: "cos" | "l2"; index?: "exact" | { codesize?: number; mode: "ann"; nbucket?: number; quantizer?: "pq" | "opq" | "bq"; }; }

A vector index's options, for a field the model declares type = "vector". The index lives on the device (on: "device", the default for this kind); the server stores and transfers the field's values but never searches them.

body.vector.distance? ​

"cos" | "l2"

How nearness is measured: cosine or Euclidean distance.

body.vector.index? ​

"exact" | { codesize?: number; mode: "ann"; nbucket?: number; quantizer?: "pq" | "opq" | "bq"; }

"exact" (the default) compares every vector; { mode: "ann", ... } an approximate index.

db3Id ​

string | number

db3.create — POST /db3. Create a db3

Parameters ​
args ​
body ​

{ custodian?: string; id?: string; metadata?: Record<string, unknown>; sync?: boolean; tags?: string[]; title: string; type?: string; }

body.custodian? ​

string

Who holds the db3: app or user:<userId>, a member of the app. Only an app owner or admin, or a server function, names one (a function names app only while it declares db3:transfer). Omitted, the caller holds it (a server function's caller; the app for a console admin).

body.id? ​

string

Keep this id instead of minting one: a ULID (26 uppercase Crockford base32 characters, the first 0 to 7) whose timestamp is no later than now plus a day, and that no document of this app holds. An app owner or admin sends one for any custodian (moving a db3 between apps); a member sends one for a db3 they hold, with no custodian named (a client creating a db3 offline). A server function never sends one.

body.metadata? ​

Record<string, unknown>

Caller-defined metadata, at most 4 KB as JSON.

body.sync? ​

boolean

false creates the db3 with sync off: no client opens it over a socket. Needs an app owner or admin, or a server function declaring db3:setSync. Omitted or true, the db3 is synced.

body.tags? ​

string[]

At most ten. A db3 tag is 1 to 48 characters, each one of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ or -, and is not ROOT_TAG. Each is taken exactly as given; nothing is trimmed.

body.title ​

string

At most 255 characters.

body.type? ​

string

A db3 type of this app: its current revision is installed before the db3 answers, so the first write already meets it.

Returns ​

Promise<{ createdAt: string; createdBy: string; custodian: string; id: string; metadata?: Record<string, unknown>; modifiedAt: string; sync: boolean; tags: string[]; title: string; type: string; }>

A record-log (format 3) document's load: when the load's epoch is reserved — at session create (open, the default) or at commit. A write made after the reservation by a client that has seen it wins against the load's rows.

getOrCreateWithAlias(args): Promise<{ alias: { aliasKey: string; createdAt?: string; documentId: string; scope: "user" | "app"; updatedAt?: string; userId?: string; }; created: boolean; id: string; }>

Beta

db3.getOrCreateWithAlias — POST /db3/get-or-create-with-alias. Get the db3 bound to an alias, creating it if absent

Parameters ​
args ​
body ​

{ alias: { aliasKey: string; scope: "user"; userId?: string; }; aliasKey?: string; metadata?: Record<string, unknown>; name?: string; permission?: "owner" | "reader" | "read-write"; scope?: string; tags?: string[]; title?: string; type?: string; }

body.alias ​

{ aliasKey: string; scope: "user"; userId?: string; }

The alias to bind. scope must be user — app-scoped aliases were removed — and userId defaults to the caller, which only an app admin may override.

body.alias.aliasKey ​

string

body.alias.scope ​

"user"

body.alias.userId? ​

string

body.aliasKey? ​

string

Not read by the handler; use alias.aliasKey. Sending it is refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.

body.metadata? ​

Record<string, unknown>

Caller-defined metadata blob applied only when the alias is created here.

body.name? ​

string

Not read by the handler. Sending it is refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.

body.permission? ​

"owner" | "reader" | "read-write"

The alias user's level on a db3 this call creates (default owner). reader or read-write writes no owner row and one row for the alias user at that level, so a reader never holds write access; it needs an app owner or admin, a console admin, or a function declaring db3:setOwnerRow. Ignored when the alias already names a db3.

body.scope? ​

string

Not read by the handler; use alias.scope. Sending it is refused with 400 VALIDATION_FAILED.

body.tags? ​

string[]

At most ten. A db3 tag is 1 to 48 characters, each one of A-Z, a-z, 0-9, _ or -, and is not ROOT_TAG. Each is taken exactly as given; nothing is trimmed. Applied only when the alias is created here, but checked before the alias is read, so an alias that already names a db3 answers the same refusal.

body.title? ​

string

body.type? ​

string

A db3 type of this app. Creating, its current revision is installed before the db3 answers; on an alias that already names a db3, a db3 of another type (or of none) is refused DB3_TYPE_MISMATCH.

Returns ​

Promise<{ alias: { aliasKey: string; createdAt?: string; documentId: string; scope: "user" | "app"; updatedAt?: string; userId?: string; }; created: boolean; id: string; }>

body.options.filter? ​

Record<string, unknown>

Query filter restricting the aggregated set; on a db3 it may carry a top-level $search on a model with a text index placed server or both.

body.options.groupBy? ​

(string | { field: string; period: "month" | "quarter" | "year"; } | { contains: string; field: string; })[]

Levels to group by: field names, period levels { field, period } and, on a db3, membership levels { field, contains }. On a db3 a field name naming a StringSet field is a facet. A format-1 document refuses StringSet facet and membership grouping with a 400.

body.options.limit? ​

number

The most groups answered (a db3 only; a format-1 document refuses it). Above 10,000 is a 400, never clamped.

body.options.operations ​

object[]

One or more aggregate operations. count takes no field; sum/avg/min/max each require one.

body.options.sort? ​

{ direction: -1 | 1; field: string; }

The groups' order (a db3 only; a format-1 document refuses it): field is count, an operation key (sum_amount), a group key (has_tags_x, due_month) or a field name.

-1 | 1

string

Ordered ops, applied in one transaction (at most 1000 on a db3, 100 on a document of another format; all-or-nothing unless atomic: false).

documents.records.patch — PATCH /documents/{documentId}/records/{model}/{recordId}. Merge fields into an existing record in a document model

Parameters ​
args ​
body ​

{ data: Record<string, unknown>; options?: { condition?: Record<string, unknown>; ifNotExists?: boolean; precondition?: Record<string, unknown>; upsertOn?: string; }; requestId?: string; }

body.data ​

Record<string, unknown>

The fields to merge into the record.

body.options? ​

{ condition?: Record<string, unknown>; ifNotExists?: boolean; precondition?: Record<string, unknown>; upsertOn?: string; }

Per-write options forwarded to the document facade.

body.options.condition? ​

Record<string, unknown>

On a db3: a guard in the query filter grammar (the filter a query takes, e.g. { status: "open", n: { $lt: 5 } }). The write applies only when the record is live and matches it; otherwise it is refused 409 DB3_CONDITION_NOT_MET and nothing is written. A missing record meets no condition. An invalid one is 400 DOCUMENT_ENTRY_INVALID.

body.options.ifNotExists? ​

boolean

Save only: apply only when no record has this id; otherwise 409 CONDITION_NOT_MET.

body.options.precondition? ​

Record<string, unknown>

Field-equality map the live record must hold; a mismatch or a missing record is 409 CONDITION_NOT_MET.

body.options.upsertOn? ​

string

Save only: land on the live record holding the same key instead of creating one. On a db3 it names a unique constraint of the model (<model>_<field>_unique, a compound constraint's name or a registered unique index's) or a field; elsewhere a field.

body.requestId? ​

string

Optional 26-char uppercase Crockford ULID naming this write. On a record-log document a retry carrying an id the document already holds is answered from its first outcome and not applied again.

string | number | boolean

records.save() ​

save(args): Promise<{ appliedFields?: Record<string, unknown>; record: Record<string, unknown>; }>

documents.records.save — POST /documents/{documentId}/records/{model}. Create or replace a record in a document model

Parameters ​
args ​
body ​

{ data: Record<string, unknown>; id: string; options?: { condition?: Record<string, unknown>; ifNotExists?: boolean; precondition?: Record<string, unknown>; upsertOn?: string; }; requestId?: string; }

body.data ​

Record<string, unknown>

The record's fields.

body.id ​

string

The record's id. Must not contain the reserved key separator.

body.options? ​

{ condition?: Record<string, unknown>; ifNotExists?: boolean; precondition?: Record<string, unknown>; upsertOn?: string; }

Per-write options forwarded to the document facade.

body.options.condition? ​

Record<string, unknown>

On a db3: a guard in the query filter grammar (the filter a query takes, e.g. { status: "open", n: { $lt: 5 } }). The write applies only when the record is live and matches it; otherwise it is refused 409 DB3_CONDITION_NOT_MET and nothing is written. A missing record meets no condition. An invalid one is 400 DOCUMENT_ENTRY_INVALID.

body.options.ifNotExists? ​

boolean

Save only: apply only when no record has this id; otherwise 409 CONDITION_NOT_MET.

body.options.precondition? ​

Record<string, unknown>

Field-equality map the live record must hold; a mismatch or a missing record is 409 CONDITION_NOT_MET.

body.options.upsertOn? ​

string

Save only: land on the live record holding the same key instead of creating one. On a db3 it names a unique constraint of the model (<model>_<field>_unique, a compound constraint's name or a registered unique index's) or a field; elsewhere a field.

body.requestId? ​

string

Optional 26-char uppercase Crockford ULID naming this write. On a record-log document a retry carrying an id the document already holds is answered from its first outcome and not applied again.

documentFormat? ​

string | number | boolean

documentId ​

string | number

model ​

string | number

Returns ​

Promise<{ appliedFields?: Record<string, unknown>; record: Record<string, unknown>; }>

args ​

body.mode? ​

"merge" | "refresh"

A record-log (format 3) document's load: merge (the default) applies the rows; refresh also deletes every record of the models the load covers that no row names.

body.models? ​

string[]

A refresh only: models to empty beside those the chunks carry, including when the session has no chunk.

body.reserveEpoch? ​

"open" | "commit"

A record-log (format 3) document's load: when the load's epoch is reserved — at session create (open, the default) or at commit. A write made after the reservation by a client that has seen it wins against the load's rows.

string | number
